hero.title: Rename hundreds of files. See every new name first.
hero.lede: Stack simple find-and-replace rules, check the live preview, and rename in one click. Not a regex person? Describe what you want and the AI assistant writes the rules.
hero.meta: Free and open source for macOS, Windows and Linux.
hero.screenshotAlt: Renamix with two rules and a live before-and-after preview of twelve photos

playground.title: Try a rule right here
playground.lede: Type a pattern or pick an example. The preview below works just like the one in the app: you see the result before anything is renamed.
playground.replacePlaceholder: Leave empty to delete the match

features.title: Everything you need, nothing that gets in the way
features.lede: Renamix stays out of your way for quick fixes and scales up to messy folders with thousands of files.

preview.title: A preview you can trust
preview.body: Rules run top to bottom like a pipeline. Every new name is shown with what's removed and added, so surprises happen on screen instead of on disk.
preview.p1: Regex or plain text, plus ignore case
preview.p2: Sequence numbers, capture groups and quick templates
preview.p3: Conflicts and invalid names are flagged before you rename
preview.alt: Cleaning up messy document names with three rules

safe.title: Safe by design
safe.body: A rename runs as one transaction. If any file fails, everything goes back the way it was. Nothing is ever overwritten.
safe.p1: Swaps, number shifts and case-only renames just work
safe.p2: Undo the last batch with one shortcut
safe.p3: Every batch is logged; reload its rules or export CSV or JSON
safe.alt: Rename history showing each file before and after

ai.title: Describe it, get the rules
ai.body: Tell the assistant what you want in your own words. It looks at your filenames, writes the rules, and shows them for you to apply or revert.
ai.p1: Use the Claude Code, Codex or Grok CLI you already have
ai.p2: Or bring a Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic or local Ollama key
ai.p3: Only your message, rules and up to 30 filenames are sent, never file contents
ai.alt: AI assistant suggesting rules that rename camera photos

plugins.title: Plugins for the special cases
plugins.body: Convert Simplified and Traditional Chinese, name photos by their EXIF data, and more. Install from the marketplace in one click.
plugins.p1: Each plugin runs in an isolated sandbox
plugins.p2: You see the permissions it asks for before installing
plugins.p3: Open format, so you can write your own

s1.title: Add files
s1.body: Drag in files or folders, or pick them from a dialog.

s2.title: Add rules
s2.body: Type what to find and what to put instead, or start from a template.

s3.title: Check the preview
s3.body: Every new name appears right away, with problems marked.

s4.title: Rename
s4.body: Apply in place or write renamed copies. Undo anytime.

q1.a: Yes. It's open source under the MIT license, with no account, ads or tracking.

q2.q: Do I need to know regular expressions?
q2.a: No. Plain text replacement and templates cover most jobs, the built-in guide explains the basics, and the AI assistant can write regex for you.

q3.q: What if a rename goes wrong?
q3.a: Check the preview first; conflicts are flagged before you start. If something still isn't right, undo the last batch, or reload any past batch's rules from the history.

q4.q: Does the AI see my files?
q4.a: Only when you ask it something, and only your message, the current rules and up to 30 filenames. File contents are never sent. With a CLI, the request goes through the tool you already use.

q5.a: Claude Code, Codex and Grok CLIs, plus Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic and local Ollama with your own key. Keys stay on your computer.

q6.a: Plugins run in an isolated sandbox and can only use the permissions they declare, such as network access or reading the files you added. You approve those before installing.

footer.tagline: A batch file renamer with regex, plugins and AI. Formerly Regex Batch Renamer.

support.title: Renamix is free and always will be
support.body: It's built and maintained in spare time. If it saves you an afternoon of renaming, a coffee helps keep it going.
